content.text: The PittCast & crewUser reviewsEpisode aired Jan 29, 2026TV-MA49mWith a nearby hospital shuttered on the busiest day of the year, Robby and team must field extra patients, including the victim of a parkour mishap.With a nearby hospital shuttered on the busiest day of the year, Robby and team must field extra patients, including the victim of a parkour mishap.With a nearby hospital shuttered on the busiest day of the year, Robby and team must field extra patients, including the victim of a parkour mishap.12User reviews7Critic reviewsFeatured reviewsStop Showing Psychiatrists as TherapistsHollywood has always taken a lot of liberty when portraying what psychiatrists do. Psychiatrists don't do therapy with patients. Psychiatrists are medical doctors who diagnose medical conditions like depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar. In no world is a psychiatrist going to sit in an ER and do therapy with one of his colleagues. It was down right annoying to see. Psychologists are PhD's and they do therapy but you would not see them in an ER. For a show that is so realistic, this betrayal did not fly. Normally, I love this show, but this episode dragged.Slightly Better...So I moved it up a notch to a 6. There was much more for Dr Langdon (Patrick Bell) to do this week and his personality is starting to show again. Something I criticized previously. Also, Dr Whitaker, not only the best of the young doctors, but also the best actor (Gerran Howell) of the young doctors, had an excellent episode. Santos got her beads read and that always gets a thumbs up from me! Again, No Dr Abbott (Shawn Hatosy) big mistake!Pounding action.This is the best episode of the season so far.I don't want to spoil anything specific, but this episode had some of the best sound mixing of the show, one particularly intense moment had the alarms that just made everything feel incredible as they worked on the patient.This episode also had one of the best depictions of CPR I've ever seen in TV medicine. Ever.This episode continues to show the truths of medicine, unapologetically. For that, I thank it.P. S. Dr King and Dr Whittaker are both royalty in my heart.Im trying to stay engagedSo, yes, I am one of the people who binged season One. In fact, I downloaded and pay for HBO Max For this show and this show alone. With that being said, I feel like season 2 is off to a very slow start. So it is seemingly one year later And you could tell, there's been a lot of transition. I'm disappointed that Dr. Collins is no longer on the show. I really liked her. Also I am curious how things are going between Whitaker and Santos living situation? Are we going to get a peek into that? Robbie seems great. Sounds like he's gonna go on a sabbatical. I am not feeling the new head doctor at all. There is also a very weird situation between Robi and an administrative person. Are they dating or what is going on? I just feel like I have more questions than answers at this point. And it is very, very slow. Then there is the setup that they are preparing us for with the other hospital shutting down... while intense I know it will be, It just doesn't seem that it will hold the same weight as the first catastrophe in season one. One of the things that was great about season One was all of the waiting room, scenes and seeing people Before & After they were treated by the doctors. We don't seem to be getting a lot of that at all. I really hope I'm wrong. But season 2 is just not doing it for me.Character Beats Land While Tension Rises NaturallyEp 4 picks up the pace without overplaying its hand, delivering improved character development alongside the show's trademark realism.The parkour patient storyline strikes the right balance between realistic medical consequences and dark humour, offering a refreshing break from pure drama. Watching overconfident students get humbled through their mistakes feels earned rather than forced, and the episode smartly uses these failures as teaching moments.The influx from the hospital closure creates steady pressure without overwhelming the narrative. Staff dynamics continue evolving naturally, with grudges thawing and new working relationships finding their footing.7./10: a solid hour that builds tension gradually while delivering satisfying character beats and a few genuinely funny moments amid the medical chaos.Related interestsContribute to this pageSuggest an edit or add missing contentEdit pageMore to explore
